options.metric: Annual number of motorist deaths and annual number of cyclist deaths
options.reason: A paired annual time series makes both the size and year-to-year movement of the two death counts directly comparable.
options.answer: Motorist deaths exceeded cyclist deaths in every year, peaking at 139 versus 29 in 2020; in 2025 the totals were 81 versus 23.
options.interpretation: This framing answers how many motorists and cyclists were killed in each year and shows the gap in their annual totals over time. Comparing both counts on the same scale is a defensible direct comparison, but it does not measure per-capita or per-mile risk.

options.metric: Annual motorist deaths minus annual cyclist deaths
options.reason: The annual count difference makes the size and direction of the mortality gap easy to read year by year.
options.answer: Motorist deaths were higher every year, by 51 to 115 deaths; the largest gap was 115 in 2021 and the smallest was 51 in 2019.
options.interpretation: This framing answers how large the annual difference between motorist and cyclist deaths was and whether either count was higher. The signed count gap is a defensible summary of their absolute comparison, but it does not display the two underlying annual totals or show per-capita or per-mile risk.
